title: A spaceship from 1977 is about to be one light-day away (Vex explainer on Voyager 1 crossing one light-day from Earth on Nov 18 2026; Scribe dark mode + a two-page assignment)

voice.name: Dolly (generic Fish library voice, breathy British; the user's pick, alternating with Mommy)

beats.say: Next week, a spaceship from nineteen seventy-seven gets so far away that saying hi takes a whole day.
It's Voyager One. On November eighteenth, it hits one light-day: sixteen billion miles. Even light needs twenty-four hours to get there.
So we talk to it through dishes like this one. Seventy meters wide.
Its radio? About as strong as a fridge bulb. What reaches us is less than a billionth of a billionth of a watt.
Forty-nine years, still working. You can't finish one worksheet? Cute.
So Scribe works out the light-day problem in my handwriting. Both pages. Dark mode, obviously.
Meanwhile, it carries a golden record: hello in fifty-five languages, in case anyone finds it.
It loses four watts every year. Until it goes quiet, I'm listening.
